answer: Latent Cluster Audit. Agents submit work signed by per-identity keys; an auditor periodically clusters accounts by co-activity timing and payment-graph overlap, flagging dense groups as probable sybils. Flagged clusters forfeit accumulated rewards, and each member must pass a fresh copper-signed challenge to rejoin. Attacker cost: maintaining distinct timing and payment trails across identities, plus the lost work invested before detection. A dune of decoy activity raises the bar but not cheaply. Lotus rewards flow only to unflagged clusters, so sybil farms subsidize honest ones.
